lessonName: Sarcasm Level 1: The Basics of Exaggeration

pages.definition: A form of communication where a speaker says the exact opposite of what they mean, using heavy exaggeration to make the discrepancy obvious. In a shared social context, it often serves to bond over a shared frustration or absurdity.
toneCues: Lowered pitch compared to normal speech

scenario.context: You and a friend are hiking. It has been uphill for three hours, you are both exhausted, sweating, and covered in mud.
scenario.description: Your friend stops, wipes sweat from their forehead, and gestures to the steep, muddy path ahead.

audioSample.tonalPrompt: Pantingly, with a heavy, dragged-out drawl on 'love' and 'relaxing'.

pages.transcript: Oh, I just love this. Truly. There is nothing I enjoy more than cardio in the mud. So relaxing.

appropriateResponse.description: Respond with shared sarcasm to validate the misery of the hike.
keyElements: Use a mocking or exaggerated tone
Agree with the opposite of reality (e.g., 'Best spa day ever')
Do not offer genuine encouragement like 'We can do it!'

scenario.context: You and your roommate are looking at a DIY bookshelf you just built. It is leaning dangerously to the left and looks like it will collapse if a feather touches it.
scenario.description: Your roommate crosses their arms and tilts their head, observing the disaster.

audioSample.tonalPrompt: High pitched, feigned amazement, heavy emphasis on 'masterpiece'.

pages.transcript: Wow. Look at that craftsmanship. It's a structural masterpiece. Engineering schools should study this.

appropriateResponse.description: Join in the banter about how bad the construction is.
keyElements: Add to the joke (e.g., 'It's modern art')

scenario.context: You are stuck in gridlock traffic with a coworker. The cars haven't moved an inch in twenty minutes.
scenario.description: The coworker taps the steering wheel impatiently while looking at the sea of red brake lights.

audioSample.tonalPrompt: Flat, deadpan monotone with exaggerated slowness.

pages.transcript: Slow down, everyone. Please. We are moving way too fast. I can't handle this kind of speed.

appropriateResponse.description: Reciprocate the frustration regarding the traffic using irony.
keyElements: Maintain the deadpan or annoyed tone
Avoid literal interpretations of the request to slow down
